newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean fishmeal exports rise Jan-Aug.
newsitem.headline: Chilean fishmeal exports rise Jan-Aug.

text.p: Chilean fishmeal exports rose 5.8 percent by value in the first eight months of this year over the same period last year, due to higher world prices, the government said.

Total fish exports, including fishmeal, came to 6.01 million tonnes in the first eight months of the year, off 10.6 percent from the same period of 1995, said the government's Fishing Undersecretariat in a report.
By value, fish exports were virtually unchanged at $1.23 billion in the first eight months of the year, it said.

The report gave no figures for fishmeal but said the product, used as animal feed, accounted for 36 percent of total exports by value and that they rose 5.8 percent in the first eight months of the year.
Higher prices accounted for all of the increase as volume of fishmeal exports actually fell slightly, the report said.
Japan was the biggest buyer of Chilean fishmeal in the first eight months of the year, accounting for 23 percent, while Taiwan was next at 20 percent, the report said.
